L1@P0: STABLE MODIFICATION OF RELATIVE CURVES
L2@P0: MICHAEL TEMKIN
L3@P0: Abstract. We generalize theorems of Deligne-Mumford and de Jong on semistable modifications of families of proper curves. The main result states that
L4@P0: after a generically ´etale alteration of the base any (not necessarily proper)
L5@P0: family of multipointed curves with semi-stable generic fiber admits a minimal
L6@P0: semi-stable modification. The latter can also be characterized by the property
L7@P0: that its geometric fibers have no certain exceptional components. The main
L8@P0: step of our proof is uniformization of one-dimensional extensions of valued
L9@P0: fields. Riemann-Zariski spaces are then used to obtain the result over any
L10@P0: integral base.

L16@P0: theorem plays a key role in the proof of properness of the moduli space of stable npointed curves of genus g. In its turn, the latter implies the following generalization

L247@P3: 1.3. Overview. Our proof of the stable modification theorem originates in nonArchimedean analytic geometry. Namely, the stable reduction theorem of DeligneMumford (in the form of Bosch-L¨utkebohmert [BL1]) was used in [Ber1, §4.3] and
L248@P3: [Ber2, §3.6] to give a local description of smooth analytic curves. On the other
L249@P3: hand, it was clear to experts that the stable reduction theorem is a consequence of
L250@P3: such a description and that the latter is actually of a very elementary nature and
L251@P3: would follow from a description of certain extensions of analytic fields (i.e. complete
L252@P3: valued fields of height one).
L253@P3: In general outline, our proof goes as follows. The core is Theorem 6.3.1 which
L254@P3: provides a description of extensions of analytic fields K/k with k algebraically closed
L255@P3: (or, more generally, deeply ramified in the sense of Assumption 6.2.1) and K the
L256@P3: completion of a finitely generated field of transcendence degree one over k. Since
L257@P3: some readers may be interested in following the algebra-geometric arguments with
L258@P3: taking the non-archimedean analytic results as a black box, we build our exposition
L259@P3: accordingly. In §2 we formulate the only analytic black box we need. This is
L260@P3: Theorem 2.1.10, which is a light version of Theorem 6.3.1. Then we postpone until
L261@P3: §6 any work involving non-archimedean analytic geometry. As a next step in the
L262@P3: paper, we deduce Theorem 2.1.8 from (temporarily black boxed) Theorem 2.1.10.
L263@P3: Theorem 2.1.8 is the main result of §2 and it describes general extensions of valued
L264@P3: fields of transcendence degree one.

L266@P3: field k is algebraically closed. It was known to experts that in this case the uniformization of valued fields is equivalent (up to some work) to the stable reduction
L267@P3: theorem. We prove uniformization directly, thus obtaining a new proof of the stable
L268@P3: reduction theorem. On the other side, one could use the stable reduction (over general valuation rings!) to get an indirect proof of Theorem 2.1.8. This would shorten
L269@P3: our argument, nearly by eliminating long but elementary §6. Note for the sake of
L270@P3: comparison that the only known alternative method for proving stable reduction
L271@P3: theorem in such generality is by use of moduli spaces of curves (so this involves
L272@P3: stable reduction over a DVR, Hilbert schemes, GIT and/or DM stacks, etc.).

L24: 【8†Lemma 37.53.6.】 Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume
L25:   1. $f$ is proper,
L26: 
L27:   2. $S$ is integral with generic point $\xi $,
L28: 
L29:   3. $S$ is normal,
L30: 
L31:   4. $X$ is reduced,
L32: 
L33:   5. every generic point of an irreducible component of $X$ maps to $\xi $,
L34: 
L35:   6. we have $H^0(X_\xi , \mathcal{O}) = \kappa (\xi )$.
L36: 
L37: Then $f_*\mathcal{O}_ X = \mathcal{O}_ S$ and $f$ has geometrically connected fibres.
L38: Proof. Apply Theorem 【10†37.53.5】 to get a factorization $X \to S' \to S$. It is enough to show that $S' = S$. This will follow from Morphisms, Lemma 【15†29.55.8】. Namely, $S'$ is reduced because $X$ is reduced (Morphisms, Lemma 【16†29.54.8】). The morphism $S' \to S$ is integral by the theorem cited above. Every generic point of $S'$ lies over $\xi $ by Morphisms, Lemma 【17†29.54.9】 and assumption (5).
L39: On the other hand, since $S'$ is the relative spectrum of $f_*\mathcal{O}_ X$ we see that the scheme theoretic fibre $S'_\xi $ is the spectrum of $H^0(X_\xi , \mathcal{O})$ which is equal to $\kappa (\xi )$ by assumption. Hence $S'$ is an integral scheme with function field equal to the function field of $S$. This finishes the proof. $\square$

L22: 【8†Lemma 29.55.12.】 Let $X$ be an irreducible, geometrically unibranch scheme. The normalization morphism $\nu : X^\nu \to X$ is a universal homeomorphism.
L23: Proof. We have to show that $\nu $ is integral, universally injective, and surjective, see Lemma 【14†29.46.5】. By Lemma 【15†29.55.5】 the morphism $\nu $ is integral. Let $x \in X$ and set $A = \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$. Since $X$ is irreducible we see that $A$ has a single minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ and $A_{red} = A/\mathfrak p$. By Lemma 【16†29.55.4】 the stalk $A' = (\nu _*\mathcal{O}_{X^\nu })_ x$ is the integral closure of $A$ in the fraction field of $A_{red}$.

Hence $\nu $ is bijective (hence surjective) and universally injective by Lemma 【18†29.10.2】. $\square$
